findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: DMARC record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy=none, pct=100, rua=true

findings.deal_impact: Spoofed mail could enable BEC/wire fraud and erode customer trust; remediation is low-cost but requires mail-flow validation before close.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject, validating all senders and DKIM/SPF alignment.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: SPF record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier=~all, lookup_count=2

findings.deal_impact: Soft-fail SPF weakens spoofing protection and compounds the DMARC monitoring-only posture.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders, then change SPF qualifier from ~all to -all.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled

evidence.excerpt: DS query for brightwaterfleet.example returned enabled=false, indicating DNSSEC is not enabled.

findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS modestly increases spoofing/cache-poisoning risk; typically a straightforward registrar/DNS fix.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at the registrar/DNS provider and verify the DS record chain.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: Risky hostname pattern vpn; first_seen 2023-02-11, last_seen 2026-09-30; risky_hostnames_count=4
Risky hostname pattern jenkins|old; first_seen 2021-06-03, last_seen 2026-08-14
Risky hostname pattern staging; first_seen 2024-01-20, last_seen 2026-10-01
Risky hostname pattern legacy; first_seen 2019-11-05, last_seen 2026-07-22

findings.deal_impact: VPN, legacy, staging and old Jenkins names suggest attack surface needing validation; could indicate unpatched or weakly protected systems.

remediation.summary: Validate ownership and exposure of each risky hostname, remove/decommission unused systems, and restrict admin access.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size

evidence.excerpt: Certificate Transparency query returned unique_hostnames=47, exceeding the 40-hostname rule threshold for a 201-1000 employee company.

findings.deal_impact: A 47-hostname footprint suggests possible asset sprawl and incomplete inventory, increasing diligence scope modestly.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames to an asset inventory and remove orphaned certificates/hosts.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support TLSv1.0=true, TLSv1.1=true, TLSv1.2=true; tls_versions=[TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www may fail customer/compliance requirements and weaken transport security.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1, retaining TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 only.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: Header strict-transport-security is null on https://brightwaterfleet.example/ (status 200).
Header strict-transport-security is null on https://www.brightwaterfleet.example/ (status 200).

findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS allows downgrade to HTTP on first visits; low-cost header fix with limited deal risk alone.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security header on apex and www after confirming HTTPS coverage.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: Potential exposure: KEV match CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, ExampleGate SSL-VPN version 7.0.11, match_tier=appliance_exposed, match_level=product; note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified. Snapshot 2026-10-20.
Fingerprint product ExampleGate SSL-VPN version 7.0.11, kind appliance, source asset_path on www host.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure of an internet-facing VPN appliance in KEV could enable intrusion; urgent patch/version verification should be a pre-close diligence item.

remediation.summary: Verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN version/patch against KEV, patch or isolate immediately if affected, and review appliance logs.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. Entity match exact; disclosed_within_months=14.

findings.deal_impact: A breach 14 months ago affecting ~3,100 individuals raises regulatory, notification and cyber-insurance questions and may affect valuation/reserves.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident report, regulator correspondence and remediation evidence; confirm notification completion and lessons learned.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: MFA not enforced on sampled admin accounts.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: Terminated users retained active access beyond 1 business day.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: Security alerts not reviewed for 2 consecutive weeks.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: Production changes lacked documented peer approval.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided

evidence.excerpt: Report period ended 2026-03-31; 216 days before 2026-11-02.

findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 216 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-11-02.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.locator: Section 1 — Independent Service Auditor's Report, Subservice organizations; Section 3, 3.2 Infrastructure
evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy script, contradicting 'every admin, no exceptions'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, contradicting same-day automated revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 exception: for 2 weeks Nov 10-23, 2025, alerts went to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed, contradicting every alert being looked at.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record is v=DMARC1; p=none, policy=none, so DMARC is not enforced and the domain can be spoofed, contradicting full enforcement.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14 reported unauthorized access to a customer support system with ~3,100 individuals notified, contradicting never having a breach.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT presence alone doesn't prove a host is live, but legacy-portal, jenkins-old and staging hostnames have last_seen dates in Jul-Oct 2026, within 12 months, showing active maintenance and contradicting decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: Annual penetration test control had no exceptions, but 2 high-severity findings were reported in the test, contradicting 'came back clean, no highs'.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 control A1.2-01 was tested with no exceptions: production data is backed up daily to immutable storage and restore tests are performed quarterly, supporting the claim.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter was provided for the period after 2026-03-31, but management states it plans to obtain a bridge letter covering April 1, 2026 forward upon request, supporting that one can be obtained.

deal_recommendations.text: Do not sign until the ExampleGate SSL-VPN is verified, in Days 0–30, as patched or isolated and a compromise assessment has reviewed the appliance logs [F-008]. Consistent with the escalate-before-signing decision, include a bring-down of the relevant security representations at signing so the position is confirmed again before the deal becomes binding [F-008].

Commission an independent scope review of the KEV-listed VPN exposure and the surrounding external footprint, prioritised in the Days 0–30 window [F-008]. As part of the escalated full diligence, pair that technical review with independent validation of management representations rather than relying on interviews alone [C-001] [C-004] [C-005].

Seek a specific indemnity, or equivalent escrow-backed protection, for losses arising from the pre-closing incident, with the underlying incident evidence package completed in Days 31–60 [F-009]. In line with the decision to escalate before signing, confirm the indemnity covers regulatory, notification and third-party claim costs linked to the disclosed event [F-009].

Assume the known incident is likely excluded from representations and warranties coverage and structure the risk allocation accordingly [F-009]. While diligence remains escalated before signing, obtain the insurer and broker position during the Days 31–60 incident-review window so any exclusion is addressed in the documents rather than discovered after signing [F-009].

Treat standalone cyber insurance as a likely underwriting requirement and confirm insurability, limits and exclusions before close, using the Days 31–60 remediation window for the email-authentication and access-control fixes [F-001] [F-010] [F-011]. Consistent with the escalated pre-signing posture, make binding cover or a firm underwriting indication a pre-close deliverable [F-001] [F-010] [F-011].

Include a post-close covenant to complete the remaining remediation, with the access-control, monitoring, offboarding and email-authentication items scheduled for Days 31–60 and the hostname and legacy-exposure items carried through Days 61–100 [F-001] [F-010] [F-011] [F-012]. Given the escalate-before-signing decision, tie covenant reporting to evidence of closure for the incident-review and reporting-currency items as well [F-004] [F-009] [F-014].

No purchase-price adjustment is warranted on cyber-remediation cost alone, because the plan totals $142K–$643K, which is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band [F-008]. Keep the economics unchanged while using the escalated pre-signing diligence and the phased windows from Days 0–30 through After day 100 to manage execution risk instead [F-008].

narrative.executive_summary:
Bottom line: Escalate to full cyber diligence before signing [F-008]. Brightwater Fleet Systems, Inc. scores 56.8 (rating D), capped by a critical, potentially exploitable exposure [F-008], a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months [F-009], and multiple management statements contradicted by evidence [C-001] [C-005].

Key risks: A KEV-listed VPN appliance needs urgent version and compromise verification [F-008]. A breach disclosed 2025-08-14 affecting ~3,100 individuals raises regulatory, notification and insurance questions [F-009]. Identity-control exceptions affect MFA and terminated-user access [F-010] [F-011]. DMARC at p=none leaves the domain spoofable for BEC/wire fraud [F-001].

Management credibility: Of 9 statements assessed, 7 were contradicted and 2 supported, spanning access, monitoring, email, incident history and legacy systems [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005] [C-006] [C-007].

Next steps: Complete escalated diligence before signing, verify the VPN exposure first, obtain the incident file and remediation evidence, and independently validate security representations [F-008] [F-009] [F-010].
key_questions_for_management: Provide evidence of the current ExampleGate SSL-VPN version and patch status, and the results of the appliance log review [F-008].
Provide the full incident report, regulator correspondence and notification-completion evidence for the breach disclosed 2025-08-14 [F-009] [C-005].
Reconcile the statement that every admin account is behind MFA with the exception affecting 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts [C-001] [F-010].
Reconcile the statement that offboarding revokes access same day with the 3 of 15 terminated users who retained access for 6, 11 and 19 business days [C-002] [F-011].
Provide evidence that security alerts are now reviewed and triaged daily following the two-week gap in Nov 10–23, 2025 [F-012] [C-003].
Confirm the timetable and sender inventory for moving DMARC from p=none to enforcement and for tightening SPF from ~all to -all [F-001] [F-002] [C-004].

Provide a current inventory reconciling the 47 certificate hostnames, including the vpn, legacy, staging and old Jenkins systems, with decommissioning or access-restriction status for each [F-004] [F-005] [C-006].
Provide a bridge letter covering the period through 2026-11-02 and the SOC report for Nimbus Cloud Services as the carved-out infrastructure host [F-014] [F-015].

limitations: Passive outside-in assessment only; no authenticated or internal testing
KEV matches are product-level; versions not verified

exceptions.description: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.
exceptions.management_response: Management is evaluating an automated HR-to-IdP de-provisioning integration. Until then, terminations are processed manually by IT upon email notification from HR.

exceptions.description: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.
exceptions.management_response: The distribution list was corrected on November 24, 2025. Management has added a weekly check that alert routing is functioning.

exceptions.management_response: Management has updated the emergency change procedure to require post-deployment approval within 48 hours.
